sentences.text: Lactococcus lactis is described as a cornerstone of dairy fermentation, and a study of 147 globally sourced isolates found clades structured by isolation source, dairy versus plant or environmental.
Lactococcus lactis is a lactic acid-producing bacterium widely used in the food industry, and strains have also been isolated from the human gastrointestinal tract.
Members of the genus Lactococcus are Gram-positive, catalase-negative, lactic acid-producing cocci of the family Streptococcaceae, related to Streptococcus and Enterococcus.
A case report describes Lactococcus garvieae as an emerging, fish-associated zoonotic pathogen that rarely causes human infection but is increasingly linked to infective endocarditis.
Lactococcosis, an important bacterial disease of farmed fish worldwide, is reported to be caused by Lactococcus garvieae, Lactococcus formosensis and Lactococcus petauri.
